shadows.name: stamp

shadows.name: stamp-lifted

motion.name: count-up

narrative.overview: The whole site is the output of a one-person design-and-engineering bureau, presented as a stamped technical dossier. Soviet Constructivism (Rodchenko / El Lissitzky poster dynamism) meets brutalist architecture (béton brut: raw concrete, monolithic massing, exposed structure). Every project is a numbered plate, every statistic a monospace ledger row, and the math is a live figures appendix. It is an homage to the art movement and the architecture only; no political iconography, and no Cyrillic or Russian text in the UI. The system commits hard to identity while staying ruthlessly readable: text always sits on a solid color field, all generative art is quarantined inside bordered blueprint panels, depth comes only from hard zero-blur offset shadows, and corners are square everywhere. It rejects the muted, interchangeable SaaS-template look the portfolio was rebuilt away from, and never trades legibility for cleverness.
keyCharacteristics: Numbered plate dossier structure; monospace apparatus (ledgers, spec tables, plate tabs).
One oxide-red accent used as solid blocks; blueprint navy + cyan for art panels only.
Zero border-radius; hard offset stamp shadows the only source of depth.
Monumental condensed display type over a documentary-grade body face.
Readability floors are non-negotiable: solid text fields, >=18px body, WCAG AA contrast.

rules.name: The Solid-Field Rule
rules.body: Every text run sits inside an opaque rectangle of exactly one palette ground. Text never floats over the diagonal bar, the concrete texture, or any canvas.

rules.name: The Art-Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Blueprint navy and cyan appear only inside bordered schematic panels; captions ride a docked solid ink bar, and body-length copy is never set on navy.

rules.name: The Red-As-Text Rule
rules.body: Red text on light is always oxide-dark (#9e2417), never the brighter oxide (#c8331f); oxide is for large display and solid blocks only.

rules.name: The Display-Is-Headings-Only Rule
rules.body: Oswald never sets a paragraph and never runs as body or all-caps prose; paragraphs are always IBM Plex Sans.

rules.name: The 18px Floor
rules.body: Running copy is never smaller than 1.125rem (18px); mono at 0.875rem is permitted for non-prose metadata only.

rules.name: The Stamp-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The only shadow in the dossier is the hard ink offset (zero blur). If a surface needs depth, it stamps; it never glows or blurs.

rules.name: The Zero-Radius Rule
rules.body: Every corner is square; border-radius:0 is enforced globally, the single exception being the round glowing cat eyes on the contact night scene.

dos: Do keep every text run on a solid palette field; quarantine all generative art inside bordered navy schematic panels with docked ink captions.
Do set body copy in IBM Plex Sans at >=18px / 1.6 and verify WCAG AA; use oxide-dark (#9e2417) for red text on light, never the brighter oxide.
Do express depth only with the hard offset Stamp shadow (6px 6px 0 #15140f, zero blur) and a 2px ink border; keep every corner square.
Do reserve Oswald for headings and the oxide accent for solid blocks; carry the apparatus in IBM Plex Mono.
Do provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for every animation: static final values and a single composed frame.
donts: Don't let the site drift back into the muted, interchangeable SaaS-template look it was rebuilt away from.
Don't ship text that is hard to read or overdesigned; cleverness never costs legibility.
Don't use any Cyrillic / Russian text, em dashes, or GPA figures anywhere in the UI.
Don't use soft or blurred shadows, gradients, glassmorphism, or any border-radius > 0 in the core dossier (the contact night scene is the sole exception).
Don't use gradient text, side-stripe borders, the hero-metric SaaS template, or identical repeating card grids.
Don't set Oswald as paragraph text or use all-caps body copy.
